name: Gouri

lead:
Gouri is described as a Korean long-lasting skin booster built on polycaprolactone (PCL), a biodegradable polymer. PCL-based products belong to the collagen stimulator class: they are injected by clinicians and aim to support collagen production for firmer, smoother skin.
PCL breaks down more slowly than many other injectables, which is why PCL products are described as long-lasting. No published clinical studies of Gouri specifically were found, so what is known comes from its marketing category and from general PCL research.

paras: Treatment is performed in a clinic by a trained injector. Which areas and how many sessions are chosen by the clinician; patients typically see results develop over weeks as collagen builds.
Injectable products carry risks such as swelling, bruising, nodules and infection, and should be given only by qualified clinicians. Product-specific safety data for Gouri have not been found.

angle.text: Gouri is used for a firmer, smoother skin look through collagen stimulation by PCL. The effect builds gradually and is described as long-lasting.

lead: Gouri, listed with the alias DEXLEVO PCL booster, is a Korean skin booster based on polycaprolactone (PCL), a synthetic, biodegradable polyester.[1] Skin boosters of this type are injected into the skin to improve texture, firmness and glow.

PCL is used in medical implants and sutures because it degrades slowly through hydrolysis; in aesthetics, PCL microsphere fillers such as Ellanse are described as collagen stimulators that address volume loss and laxity with a long-lasting effect.[1]
No published clinical studies of Gouri itself were found.

paras: PCL degrades more slowly than polylactide and polyglycolide, which makes it suited to long-lasting uses; the FDA has approved it for devices such as sutures and drug delivery.[1]
